title: Michigan Medical Marijuana Card Benefits: Is It Worth It?
h1: Is a Michigan Medical Marijuana Card Still Worth Getting?
metaDescription: Michigan medical marijuana card benefits in an adult-use state: age, taxes, limits, caregivers and protections, plus how to apply and what to bring to a store.
excerpt: Adult-use sales changed the math, but a Michigan medical card still pays off for some people. Here's what it changes, what it costs and what to bring on your first patient visit.
keyTakeaways: Registered patients 18 and older can shop with a valid card; adult-use shopping starts at 21.
Medical sales skip the 10% excise tax, saving $10.60 in tax per $100.
The state fee is $40 for a two-year card, plus a physician's certification.
A caregiver can shop and grow for a patient, and a card plus photo ID gives legal protection.
body:
Michigan medical marijuana card benefits still matter for some people, even with adult-use stores open to anyone 21 and older. A card changes who can shop, how much tax you pay, how much you can buy and who can help you. Here's how to decide if it's worth it.

## Short answer: who still gains from a card

A card helps most if you're 18 to 20, buy often enough for tax savings to add up, need a caregiver, or want the legal protections of registration. If you're at least 21 and buy now and then, adult-use shopping may be all you need. Our guide to [buying medical vs. recreational cannabis](/blog/buying-weed-med-vs-rec/) compares the two.

## Age: patients 18 and older can shop

Adult-use shopping starts at 21. Registered patients 18 and older can buy with a valid card, and High Society welcomes them.

## Michigan medical marijuana card benefits for your budget

Adult-use purchases carry a 10% excise tax plus 6% sales tax, figured on the price including the excise. Medical sales to registered patients skip the excise.

| On a $100 purchase | Adult-use | Medical |
|---|---|---|
| 10% excise tax | $10.00 | $0 |
| 6% sales tax | $6.60 | $6.00 |
| Total tax | $16.60 | $6.00 |

At $10.60 saved per $100, about $380 in purchases over the card's two years covers the $40 state fee. The doctor's visit is a separate cost that varies by provider.

## Patient limits, home grow and legal protections

| | Registered patient | Adult-use (21+) |
|---|---|---|
| Buying | 2.5 oz a day, 10 oz a month | 2.5 oz per transaction, up to 15 g concentrate |
| Carrying | 2.5 oz of usable marijuana | 2.5 oz, up to 15 g concentrate |
| Home grow | 12 plants in a locked, enclosed space if no caregiver grows for you | 12 plants per residence, locked and out of public view |
| Edibles | Up to 50 mg THC per dose | Up to 10 mg THC per serving |

Arrest protection comes from showing a valid registry card with photo ID. A card doesn't stop a private employer from disciplining you for cannabis use. Our [Michigan cannabis laws guide](/cannabis-laws-by-state/michigan/) has the details.

## Caregivers for patients who can't shop for themselves

A registered caregiver can buy and grow for you. Caregivers must be 21 or older, agree to a criminal background check, have no disqualifying convictions and hold a caregiver card for each patient. One caregiver can help up to five patients, and each patient can have only one caregiver. To name one, use the paper application; there's no separate caregiver fee.

## Getting certified: conditions, physician and registry

Michigan's qualifying conditions include cancer, PTSD, chronic pain, arthritis, glaucoma and Crohn's disease, among others. A Michigan-licensed MD or DO certifies you after an evaluation, which the state's online instructions say must be within the past six months. You then apply to the state registry online, or on paper if you're naming a caregiver. Cards go only to Michigan residents and last two years. Our [medical card guide](/getting-a-medical-card/) covers each step.

## A first patient visit at High Society

Bring your registry card and a valid photo ID; Michigan stores check ID before every sale. You'll check in at the front desk, a budtender will help you choose, and a staff member will take payment and review your order. Cash works, and other payment options vary by store. If you'd like to order ahead, ask your store how pickup works for patients. [Find your nearest store](/dispensary-locations/) or browse our [dispensary FAQ](/faq/).

## Out-of-state use: what reciprocity does and doesn't cover

Michigan honors valid cards from other states at licensed provisioning centers, but your Michigan card works elsewhere only where that state allows it. Never take cannabis across state lines. Our guide to [medical marijuana reciprocity](/blog/medical-marijuana-card-reciprocity/) explains how states differ.

faq.q: Is a medical card required to buy cannabis in Michigan?
faq.a: No, not if you're 21 or older. At that age, government-issued photo ID is all you need to shop adult-use. A card matters if you're 18 to 20, want to skip the 10% excise tax, need a caregiver or want the legal protections that come with registration.

faq.q: How much does a Michigan medical marijuana card cost?
faq.a: The state fee is $40, and renewing costs the same. Online applicants can pay by credit card or electronic check, and paper applicants send a check or money order. Your physician's evaluation is a separate cost that varies by provider. Each card lasts two years.

faq.q: Can an 18-year-old buy cannabis in Michigan with a medical card?
faq.a: Yes. Registered patients 18 and older can buy with a valid registry card and photo ID, and High Society welcomes medical patients 18 and older with a valid card. Without a card, shopping is for adults 21 and older. Patients under 18 need a parent or guardian as their caregiver.
